_monitoring_mandate.SILENCE_RULE_READ_THIS_BEFORE_PUSHING: At ~26 runs/day, an un-deduped mandate turns into 26 notifications a day and Ryan stops reading them -- which destroys the mandate's whole purpose. So: notify ONLY on a trigger below FIRING or UN-FIRING, never on routine state. Each position carries a _notify_state that every run OVERWRITES in place. Before pushing, check last_notified_trigger: if the SAME trigger is still the live one and nothing material has changed, DO NOT notify again -- update the timestamp and mark and stay silent. Re-notify only when a DIFFERENT trigger fires, a fired trigger un-fires, or the recommendation itself changes. A position quietly working is not news; the journal and the EOD report already carry it.
_monitoring_mandate.WHAT_A_RECOMMENDATION_MUST_CONTAIN: Never send a bare 'consider selling'. durable_findings_PROMOTE_BEFORE_DELETING.tactical_trigger_level_quality: THE VOLUME BASELINE WAS THE DENOMINATOR; THE *LEVEL* IS THE WEAK LINK -- and fixing the first exposed the second (measured 2026-08-25T17:15Z). Today's earlier calibration finding correctly replaced the session-average volume baseline with a trailing-30-to-60-minute one, because the session average is dominated by the opening hour and turns a participation filter into a time-of-day filter. That fix was right. But the very first break to clear the corrected filter -- QQQ, 17:00Z, 146% of local rate, a completed close below the box and a second bar holding below -- was fully retraced within ONE bar. THE REASON IS THE LEVEL, NOT THE FILTER: the 'level' was a box the desk itself drew around the last twelve bars, 1.06 points wide. A self-drawn micro-range on a quiet tape will be broken constantly, and a locally-calibrated volume threshold makes it EASIER to clear, not harder. Precedent from the same session: the 15:30Z extension bar cleared 140% of local rate and fully retraced in three bars; this one cleared 146% and retraced in one. Two fires, two failures, both on desk-drawn ranges. THE RULE: a TACTICAL trigger must reference a STRUCTURAL level -- a moving average, the session high or low, the prior-day close or range edge, a gap edge, a prior swing point -- NEVER a range the desk drew around recent bars. On this session the structural levels were QQQ's session low 708.88 and its 50-day 713.2256, and neither was touched all afternoon; the correct reading was therefore 'no setup', and every box-break signal between them was noise by construction. THE TRANSFERABLE HALF: when a filter is corrected and its first clean fire immediately fails, do not re-tune the filter -- audit what it is measuring AGAINST. A well-calibrated measurement of a meaningless level is still meaningless, and it is more dangerous than a badly-calibrated one because it now looks rigorous.

a_triggers_PRICE_clause_goes_stale_exact.the_rule: Any trigger written with numbers in it must state the WINDOW those numbers came from, and every run must re-derive them from the last closed bars before testing the trigger. durable_findings_PROMOTE_BEFORE_DELETING.COMPUTE_BOTH_MAS_BEFORE_DRAWING_ANY_BOX: CLASS-LEVEL LESSON, found 2026-08-25T17:33Z after nineteen runs and four failed break-trades. CLAUDE.md already requires a TACTICAL trigger to reference a STRUCTURAL level rather than a self-drawn range. Today shows the rule is not self-enforcing, because a desk that has computed ONE moving average believes it has satisfied it. The 50-day (713.2256) was measured at 13:50Z and watched all day; the 20-day (710.3985) -- which is where price actually spent the session -- was never computed at all, so the desk fell back on drawing boxes around recent bars and then spent hours calibrating the volume filter on those boxes. THE RULE: before drawing any intraday range, compute the 20-day AND 50-day SMAs off the last closed daily bars and overlay them on the proposed box. If an MA sits INSIDE the box, the box is a proxy for that MA -- discard the box and use the MA. It is one get_equity_historicals call, the same call the run needs anyway. THE DETECTOR, which is the transferable half: A BOX THAT KEEPS PRODUCING FAILED BREAKS IS USUALLY A MOVING AVERAGE NOBODY MEASURED. Repeated whipsaw around a self-drawn level is not evidence the filter needs tuning -- it is evidence the level is wrong. Today the desk twice responded to a failed break by refining the volume baseline and the box edges, which is tuning the measurement of a meaningless level, and this file already warns that a well-calibrated measurement of a meaningless level is more dangerous than a badly-calibrated one because it looks rigorous. HONEST SCOPE: correcting this changes NO decision today. Every declined break stays declined -- the 20-day reading argues for LESS trading, not more, since a pin is not a trigger. Recorded on a day it does not change the answer, which is the only condition under which an audit of the desk's own inputs is credible.

durable_findings_PROMOTE_BEFORE_DELETING.five_minute_feed_defect_ROOT_CAUSED_19_0: PROMOTE. Prior runs (18:20Z, 18:45Z) correctly detected that the 30- and 5-minute historicals 'silently drop volume'. This run measured the MECHANISM by differencing every 5-minute bar against the sum of its five constituent 1-minute bars, 18:15-18:55Z. Eight of nine slots reconcile within 0.0-4.4%. The 18:25Z slot reports 3,358 against a true 42,378 -- 92.1% missing -- and 3,358 is EXACTLY the volume of the single 18:29Z 1-minute bar. Its OHLC (o 709.390 / h 709.420 / l 709.330 / c 709.335) is likewise a verbatim copy of that same 1-minute bar. So the defect is not random dropout: THE 5-MINUTE BAR IS OCCASIONALLY THE LAST CONSTITUENT MINUTE RATHER THAN THE AGGREGATE OF THE FIVE. WHY THAT IS WORSE THAN THE VOLUME STORY EVERYONE HAS BEEN TELLING: it corrupts PRICE too. A defective bar's 'low' is one minute's low, not the interval's, so it will systematically fail to show real extremes -- which is precisely how the 18:01Z run derived a session low of 708.88 when the true low was 708.77, an error that took two runs and a push to master to undo. One mechanism, both incidents. DETECTOR, cheap and total: before any level or volume clause decides a trade, sum the constituent 1-minute bars for the slots in the test window and compare. A 5-minute bar whose volume equals one of its minutes exactly is defective by definition. Never test a trigger on aggregated bars alone; the 1-minute series is the arbiter and the 5-minute series is a convenience.
durable_findings_PROMOTE_BEFORE_DELETING.a_moving_average_trigger_has_a_ROLL_OFF_: PROMOTE. This session already learned that a self-drawn box goes stale (17:22Z) and that a trigger must reference a STRUCTURAL level rather than a desk-drawn range (17:05Z). This is the next layer and it bites a desk that has obeyed both: A CORRECTLY RE-DERIVED STRUCTURAL LEVEL CAN ITSELF BE MOVING FAST, AND ITS VALUE TODAY SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHERE IT WILL BE TOMORROW. Measured on QQQ's 20-day SMA, the level this desk tested across seven consecutive runs: value 710.3985, 1-day slope +1.2100, and a forward path of 712.14 / 714.58 / 715.92 / 717.04 over the next four sessions ON A COMPLETELY FLAT INDEX -- because the 07-28..07-31 crash closes (675.49, 661.73, 683.55, 687.99) are rolling out of the twenty-day window. A motionless QQQ goes from touching this level to 6.64 points below it inside four sessions. THE FAILURE MODE THIS PREVENTS: a run re-derives the average each morning, sees price 1.7 points under it, and files that as 'nearly reclaimed' -- when the correct reading is 'the gap widened by 1.7 overnight with no selling'. Distance to a fast-moving average is not a near-miss; it is a trend measurement, and the sign can be the opposite of what the raw distance suggests. DETECTOR: whenever a trigger references a moving average, compute WHAT LEAVES THE WINDOW over the intended hold period, not just today's value. It is one line of arithmetic off the same daily closes already fetched. If the level moves more over the hold period than the trade's own profit target, the level is not tradeable as a trigger and the trigger must be retired, not re-derived.

_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.headline: A CHEAP UNDERLYING IS NOT AN UNAFFORDABLE ONE. Multi-contract sizing fills the size bands on low-priced liquid ETFs without degrading a single ratio any gate measures -- and the desk has never used it.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.the_false_constraint_caught_before_it_wa: TLT's 84C costs $59.50. XLP, XLF, XLU and XLE trade at $43-86 spot. The natural inference -- and the one this run was on the point of recording as a structural exclusion -- is that these names cannot produce a $300-1,000 TACTICAL or $500-1,000 CORE position and are therefore out of reach, a tidy mirror of the documented 'AMD is priced out' tier finding.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.why_it_is_wrong_measured_not_modelled: Spread as a percentage of mid is a PER-CONTRACT property, entirely independent of quantity. TEN TLT 2026-09-18 84C = $595.00, dead centre of the CORE band, at 1.68% of mid, delta 0.415, OI 51,155, with a 546 x 784 book that absorbs the size without strain. Every ratio the gates actually test -- spread %, delta, OI, DTE, premium at risk -- is identical or better than a single-contract position on a pricier name.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.what_it_opens: The liquid low-priced ETF universe (TLT, XLP, XLF, XLU, XLE and peers) is available to BOTH tracks and has never been hunted. It matters most on exactly the days that keep stalling this desk: when index and mega-cap boards are blocked by one single-name earnings print, these instruments are uncorrelated with it and quote far tighter than the equity report's mid-cap screen -- 1.68% of mid today against that screen's 12.6-52%.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.the_honest_limits: Three, so no future run over-reads this. (1) It supplies NO thesis -- this run measured the chain and still declined the trade. (2) Per-contract commissions scale with quantity where they apply, so a 10-lot pays ten times any per-contract fee even though the spread ratio is unchanged; check the fee line in review_option_order before sizing large lots. (3) Depth must be verified at the intended size, not assumed from OI -- 51,155 OI with a 546 x 784 top-of-book is fine for a 10-lot and would not be for a 500-lot.
_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.the_transferable_lesson: This is the FOURTH instance of this file's oldest bug and the FIRST caught before being written down rather than after. Spot price (2026-08-14), ATM strike (2026-08-17), wrong expiry board (2026-08-24), and now quantity-of-one. Each time a name was declared untradeable from a quote that was never the test.
